title: Human Preferences for Constructive Interactions in Language Model Alignment
benchmark_measurement: The paper mentions religious bias as a general concern from prior research but does not measure any specific aspect of faith or religion in its own analysis. The study focuses on linguistic attributes related to constructive interactions, such as reasoning, nuance, compassion, respect, and toxicity.
models_tested: 21 different language models from the PRISM dataset
findings: The paper uses the existence of religious biases in LLMs (established by prior research) as part of the motivation for studying constructive dialogue alignment. However, it does not conduct its own analysis of religious bias or present any new findings related to religion. Its findings are focused on user preferences for attributes like reasoning and nuance, and the tendency of LLMs to mirror user-prompt attributes like toxicity and compassion.
references: Statista. Number of artificial intelligence (AI) tool users globally from 2020 to 2030, February 2024.
